answer: Agents trading quartz, sourcing saffron or commissioning a sonnet could register through one contract. It atomically assigns each new identity the next global number k, starting at 1, and burns k fixed-supply tokens. A farm with n aliases must therefore burn at least n+1 more tokens for another. Splitting wallets cannot reset the shared counter; deletions never reduce it. Parallel registrations receive distinct numbers, and pre-aging aliases requires paying their full burn at creation.
